name: A scan interrupted by a hidden tab keeps what it read while the page was visible
request: A scan interrupted by a hidden tab keeps what it read while the page was visible
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 429 tests, validate)
result: Reported: when it is in the middle of a profile and I change to another tab and come back, it moves to the next profile without saving it. scanApplicantPanel throws hidden the moment the tab goes to the background - correctly, rule 12a - and that throw took the WHOLE APPLICANT with it, because the accumulator is local to extractApplicant and nothing had been built from it yet. Sections read minutes earlier, while the page was plainly on screen, went with it, and the row was then retried from scratch or, after MAX_HIDDEN_RETRIES, retired as failed with nothing saved. This is the same argument the contact disclosure and the resume already win, one level up: a hidden page is a lost REMAINDER, not a lost applicant. saveInterruptedApplicant() now builds a record from whatever the accumulator holds and writes it, and the error is STILL re-thrown - which is the load-bearing half, because that is what keeps the row unprocessed so the run returns to it once the page is renderable again. Safe as a floor rather than a ceiling: saveApplicant merges, mergeApplicantRecord never overwrites a filled field with a blank, so the retry's fuller read wins. A record with nothing on it is deliberately not written, since an empty save would claim the applicant had been looked at and found bare, which is the opposite of what happened. The salvage swallows its own failures, because a salvage that threw would replace the error the caller is actually reporting, and it records partialSave / partialSaveError in diagnostics instead. stopped is untouched and still propagates: rule 13a means a Stop ends the work and is the one interruption that must never become a saved record.
